title: Loneliness and Connection
summary: Loneliness, getting out and keeping in touch, people to call on, and daily purpose. Written in plain language for older adults.
clinicianNotes: Written for adults aged 60 and over. Speak slowly, offer to read items aloud, and allow extra time. Topic areas are informed by general published work on stress, mood and wellbeing. All items are original wording and are not copied or adapted from any instrument. Bands are provisional and not clinically validated. Use the summary to guide your own questions. Draft content: needs review by a licensed psychologist, and a topic-specific reference list should be added during that review.
prompt: Thinking about the last two weeks, how true is this for you?

guidance.ok: On feeling lonely, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On feeling lonely, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Ask when loneliness is strongest and what kind of company is missed.
guidance.explore: On feeling lonely, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Ask when loneliness is strongest and what kind of company is missed.

domains.label: Staying in
domains.description: Finding it hard to get out and losing touch.

guidance.ok: On staying in, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On staying in, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore practical barriers such as mobility, transport and confidence.
guidance.explore: On staying in, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore practical barriers such as mobility, transport and confidence.

domains.label: People to call on
domains.description: Having someone to turn to and regular contact.

guidance.ok: On people to call on, there is a strength to build on. Use it when planning next steps.
guidance.watch: On people to call on, support is partly in place. Explore what helps and what gets in the way. Explore who could be contacted more often.
guidance.explore: On people to call on, support looks thin. Explore what is missing, who or what could help, and small first steps. Explore who could be contacted more often.

domains.label: Daily purpose
domains.description: Feeling useful and having things to look forward to.

guidance.ok: On daily purpose, there is a strength to build on. Use it when planning next steps.
guidance.watch: On daily purpose, support is partly in place. Explore what helps and what gets in the way. Build on roles and activities that give meaning.
guidance.explore: On daily purpose, support looks thin. Explore what is missing, who or what could help, and small first steps. Build on roles and activities that give meaning.

items.text: I feel lonely or cut off from others.
Days go by with no one visiting or calling.
I miss having someone to share my day with.
I find it hard to get out of the house.
I have lost touch with friends I used to see.
I spend most of the day alone.
There is someone I can call when I need help.
Family or neighbours visit or phone regularly.
I take part in prayers, gatherings or community life.
I still have things that give my day a purpose.
I feel useful to my family or community.
I look forward to something each week.
